sentences.text:
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor representing the respondent/State.
3.

The Revenue Divisional Officer, Atmakur complained that basing on a news item alleging some misdeeds in A.P. daily news paper dated 24.09.2022, on enquiry made by the Tahasildar, Kaluvoy Mandal it came to light that compensation for acquisition of land was disbursed on issuing genuineness certificates to the beneficiaries whose lands were said to have been submerged in Chowtapalli Balancing Reservoir.

That the land is covered by reserve forest in RSR and has not been denotified nor is it converted into AW dry, nor were issued the D-form pattas issued with the approval of the Assignment Review Committee, but the names of the ryots appearing in the D-Register and the other village records were incorporated astonishing it.

Therefore, incorporations in the village records and the payment of compensation to the ineligible persons was done in an organized manner by way of fabricating the revenue records in collusion with the revenue officials,
brokers and other vested interests and thus caused huge loss to the exchequer of the Government.

4. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that insofar as the petitioner is concerned, the relevant land in S.No.1084 of Chowtapalli was given to Talla Ramana Reddy, S/o Venkat Reddy under a DKT patta vide patta No.921 vide F.Dis.No.249/94 dated 22.05.1984 and thereafter, on his death the land was sold by his son Talla Devendra Reddy to M.Poli Reddy vide document No.246/2004 dated 31.03.2004 and subsequently petitioner purchased from M.Poli Reddy in the year 2006 and obtained a sale deed on 07.03.2006 but the same was registered on 12.11.2014 on payment of deficit stamp duty.
He further submitted that meanwhile in 2011 pattadar pass book was also issued in his name on 10.02.2011.

He further submitted that the petitioner purchased the land even before issue of G.O.No.307 dated 06.06.2013 basing on which the allegation is made that as per the said G.O., NOC has to be obtained from the District Collector for purchase of ex-military person's land before the purchase.

He further submitted that as per G.O.No.1117 Revenue (Assn.I)
Department dated 11.11.1993 land assigned to any military personnel can be sold after ten years of its assignment and in this connection the learned counsel for the petitioner placed reliance on the decision of the Division Bench of this High Court in W.A.No.1451 of 2023 in the case of The District Collector, Nalgonda and others Vs K.Sreedhar Rao 1 .

1 the news paper item the report was submitted implicating all the revenue officials and the beneficiaries without proper verification.

sentences.text: In support of his arguments the copies of the documents such as the previous sale deeds and EC were also enclosed.
He further submitted that even the Forest Officials have not so far claimed that this land is covered by the reserve forest and yet a case was registered.

He further submitted that when the W.A.No.1451 of 2023 of the Division Bench of this High Court. petitioner purchased the property and his name was also mutated in the revenue record, there was no such allegation at any time.

He further submitted that Tahasildar and Forest Department as well have given NOC., as can be seen from 1) the Proceedings of the RDO, Atmakur vide RC No.774/20 dated 11.01.2021 and 2) Conservator of Forests/District Forest Officer, Nellore in Rc.No.1779/2019-F5 dated 04.02.2020 addressed to the Special Deputy Collector (L.A)., Telugu Ganga Project, Rapur at Nellore.

5. Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor submitted that as per the report, insofar as the petitioner is concerned, Talla Ramana Reddy being ex-servicemen, was granted patta No.921, dated 22.05.1984 and after his demise, the land was transferred to his wife Ramanamma Vide F.Dis No.25/95 in ROR and later M.Poli Reddy purchased the said land vide document No.246 of 2004 dated 31.03.2004 from T.Devendra Reddy and thereafter the petitioner purchased the said land vide document No.1442/2014 from M.Poli Reddy and that the web land adangal and mutual 1B with khata No.957 recorded the same.

It is further submitted that D-Register showing the grant of said land under D-form is not available in the records and that as per G.O.Ms.307 dated 06.06.2013 Collector has to issue NOC to transfer the lands from Ex-military persons and the said land was purchased in the year 2003 and hence it can be treated as patta land and that in this case, compensation for acquisition of land was also paid.
6. Perused the record.
7. As per the allegations, insofar as the petitioner is concerned, it is not prima facie shown that the petitioner has indulged in any activity of creating false document.

The question whether the said land falls within the reserve forest and whether date of patta issued way back in 1984 is valid or not is all a civil dispute and even in the report basing on which FIR was issued also the remarks are noted to the same effect and suggested action under POT Act, since assigned land under patta cannot be sold.

Therefore, insofar as this petitioner is concerned, anticipatory bail can be granted,
however subject to conditions in view of the above facts and circumstances discussed.
8. In the result, the criminal petition is allowed.

The petitioner/Gollamudi Srinivasulu Reddy (A-9)
is directed to be released on bail in the event of his arrest in Crime No. 8 of 2023 of Kaluvoy Police Station, Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore District registered on 23.01.2023 for the offences punishable under Sections 120B, 409, 420, 417, 468, 471 r/w 34 IPC on furnishing his personal bond for a sum of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees twenty five thousand only) with two sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the Station House Officer, Kaluvoy Police Station, Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore District and subject to complying the following conditions:
